source.changes: Instruction is the source's goal, word for word. Start state as in the source (flight mode on), set with `cmd connectivity airplane-mode` instead of the source's helper; setup also keeps the phone's own state and teardown puts it back. The check is the source's (settings global airplane_mode_on is 0). Needs the bench phone on USB adb: flight mode can drop a Wi-Fi adb link.

setup.why: Keep the phone's own flight-mode state once (a retried setup keeps the first copy), so teardown puts it back.
Start with flight mode on, so the agent has to turn it off.
Open Settings at its home page, whatever screen an earlier run left it on.

checks.why: settings global airplane_mode_on, which the flight mode switch writes, is 0. Setup turned flight mode on, so an agent that does nothing fails.

teardown.why: Put the phone's own flight-mode state back (off when none was saved), and drop the saved copy.

argv: f=/data/local/tmp/computer-bench-{{nonce}}.orig; [ -e $f ] || exit 0; case "$(cat $f 2>/dev/null)" in 1) cmd connectivity airplane-mode enable ;; *) cmd connectivity airplane-mode disable ;; esac; rm -f $f

oracle.why: Turn flight mode off, as the switch does.
